metadata.title: A significance test for the lasso

nodes.name: Linear regression model
nodes.statement_latex: Outcome $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and predictor matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ satisfy $y = X\beta^* + \varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I)$ and unknown $\beta^* \in \mathbb{R}^p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Gaussian linear regression model with unknown coefficient vector and i.i.d. normal errors.

nodes.name: Lasso estimator
nodes.statement_latex: $\hat{\beta} = \arg\min_{\beta \in \mathbb{R}^p} \tfrac{1}{2}\|y - X\beta\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\beta\|_1$, with tuning parameter $\lambda \geq 0$ controlling sparsity.
nodes.statement_clean: Penalized least-squares estimator with $\ell_1$ penalty.

nodes.name: General position
nodes.statement_latex: Points $X_1, \ldots, X_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are in general position if no $k$-dimensional affine subspace ($k < \min\{n,p\}$) contains more than $k+1$ elements of $\{\pm X_1, \ldots, \pm X_p\}$ excluding antipodal pairs.
nodes.statement_clean: Mild geometric genericity condition on the columns of $X$ ensuring uniqueness of the lasso solution.

nodes.name: Lasso knots and active set
nodes.statement_latex: The lasso path $\hat{\beta}(\lambda)$ is continuous and piecewise linear with knots $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_r \geq 0$; at knot $\lambda_k$ a variable enters or leaves the active set $A = \mathrm{supp}(\hat{\beta}(\lambda_k))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Knots are values of $\lambda$ at which the active set changes.

nodes.name: Reduced lasso solution $\tilde{\beta}_A$
nodes.statement_latex: $\tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1}) = \arg\min_{\beta_A \in \mathbb{R}^{|A|}} \tfrac{1}{2}\|y - X_A \beta_A\|_2^2 + \lambda_{k+1}\|\beta_A\|_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lasso solution restricted to the current active set $A$ at the next knot.

nodes.name: Covariance test statistic
nodes.statement_latex: $T_k = \bigl(\langle y, X\hat{\beta}(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle - \langle y, X_A \tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle\bigr)/\sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Inner product of $y$ with the difference of fitted values from the full and reduced lasso fits, evaluated at $\lambda_{k+1}$.

nodes.name: Chi-squared drop-in-RSS statistic
nodes.statement_latex: $R_j = (\mathrm{RSS}_M - \mathrm{RSS}_{M\cup\{j\}})/\sigma^2$, compared to a $\chi_1^2$ distribution to test the significance of variable $j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical chi-squared statistic for adding one variable to a fixed nested model.

nodes.name: Soft-thresholding operator
nodes.statement_latex: $S_\lambda(x) = (x-\lambda)$ if $x > \lambda$; $0$ if $|x|\leq \lambda$; $(x+\lambda)$ if $x < -\lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: The closed-form lasso solution for orthogonal design.

nodes.name: Degrees of freedom
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathrm{df}(\hat{y}) = \tfrac{1}{\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Cov}(y_i, \hat{y}_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum of covariances between observations and fitted values.

nodes.name: Knot recursion via join/leave events
nodes.statement_latex: $\lambda_{k+1} = \max\{\lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm{join}}, \lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm{leave}}\}$ with $\lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm{join}} = \max_{j\notin A, s\in\{-1,1\}} \frac{X_j^T(I-P_A)y}{s - X_j^T (X_A^T)^+ s_A} \cdot \mathbf{1}\{\cdot < \lambda_k\}$ and analogous formula for leave.
nodes.statement_clean: Explicit LARS recursion for the next knot in terms of join and leave times.
nodes.origin_citation: Efron et al. LARS; Tibshirani lassounique

nodes.name: Discrete-time Gaussian process $g(j,s)$
nodes.statement_latex: $g(j,s) = sU_j$ for $j=1,\ldots,p$, $s\in\{-1,1\}$, with $U_j = X_j^T y$, having covariance $\mathbb{E}[g(j,s)g(j',s')] = ss' R_{j,j'}\sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Indexed Gaussian field whose maxima encode the first lasso knot.

nodes.name: Auxiliary process $h^{(j_1,s_1)}$ and $M(j_1,s_1)$
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional process that decorrelates from $g(j_1,s_1)$ and whose maximum equals $\lambda_2$ when $j_1,s_1$ are the argmax of $g$.

nodes.name: Generalized process $g^{(A,s_A)}$
nodes.statement_latex: $g^{(A,s_A)}(j,s) = \frac{X_j^T(I-P_A)y}{s - X_j^T (X_A^T)^+ s_A}$ for $j\notin A$, $s\in\{-1,1\}$, with covariance \eqref{eqg2cov}; mean zero when $A \supseteq A^*$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discrete Gaussian process whose maximum is the next-knot statistic at a general step.

nodes.name: Auxiliary maxima $M^+, M^-, M^0$
nodes.statement_latex: Partition $(j',s')\notin A\cup\{j\}$ by sign of $1 - \Sigma_{j,j'}/\Sigma_{jj}$; $M^+$ takes the max over $\{<1\}$ indices, $M^-$ the min over $\{>1\}$, and $M^0$ a max over equality indices, of $\frac{g(j',s') - (\Sigma_{j,j'}/\Sigma_{jj}) g(j,s)}{1 - \Sigma_{j,j'}/\Sigma_{jj}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three auxiliary statistics arising from a dual representation of the argmax event.

nodes.name: Significance testing along the lasso path
nodes.statement_latex: At step $k$ of the lasso path, test $H_0: A \supseteq \mathrm{supp}(\beta^*)$, where $A$ is the active set just before knot $\lambda_k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Test whether the variable entering at the $k$th lasso knot is significant, given that $A$ already contains all truly active variables.

nodes.name: Strong-signal condition (orthogonal X)
nodes.statement_latex: $\min_{j\in A^*} |\beta_j^*| - \sigma\sqrt{2\log p} \to \infty$ as $p \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest nonzero true coefficient grows faster than $\sigma\sqrt{2\log p}$.

nodes.name: Conditional-variance bound and $|S| \gg \log p$ (general X, $k=1$)
nodes.statement_latex: For each $j$, $\exists S \subseteq \{1,\ldots,p\}\setminus\{j\}$ with $1 - R_{i,S\setminus\{i\}}(R_{S\setminus\{i\},S\setminus\{i\}})^{-1} R_{S\setminus\{i\},i} \geq \delta^2$ for all $i\in S$, and $|S| \geq d_p$ with $d_p/\log p \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional variance of $X_i^T y$ given the others in $S$ is bounded below, and $|S|$ grows faster than $\log p$.

nodes.name: Path-stability and irrepresentability conditions (general X, general step)
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathbb{P}(B) \to 1$ for the event $B$ of \eqref{eqgenxb}; $\|(X_{A_0})^+ X_j\|_1 \leq 1-\eta$ for $j\notin A_0$; diagonal entries of $R_{ij}=X_i^T(I-P_{A_0})X_j$ all of the same order; for each $j\notin A_0$ a subset $S$ satisfying the conditional-variance bound, $|R_{ij}|/R_{jj} < \eta/(2-\eta)$, and $\|(X_{A_0\cup\{j\}})^+ X_i\|_1 < 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combined model-stability, irrepresentability, and conditional-variance assumptions for the general-step result.

nodes.name: Lasso fitted-value formula
nodes.statement_latex: $X\hat{\beta}(\lambda) = P_A y - \lambda (X_A^T)^+ s_A$, where $P_A = X_A(X_A^T X_A)^{-1} X_A^T$ and $(X_A^T)^+ = X_A(X_A^T X_A)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form fitted value: projection minus shrinkage term.

nodes.name: Projection form of $T_k$
nodes.statement_latex: $T_k = y^T(P_{A\cup\{j\}} - P_A)y/\sigma^2 - \lambda_{k+1} \cdot y^T\bigl((X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A\bigr)/\sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decomposition of $T_k$ into a chi-squared term and a shrinkage-correction term.

nodes.name: F-statistic for unknown $\sigma^2$
nodes.statement_latex: $F_k = \frac{\langle y, X\hat{\beta}(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle - \langle y, X_A \tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle}{\hat{\sigma}^2} \stackrel{d}{\to} F_{2,n-p}$, with $\hat{\sigma}^2 = \|y - X\hat{\beta}^{\mathrm{LS}}\|_2^2/(n-p)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Plug-in version of $T_k$ with $\hat{\sigma}^2$ from the full-model OLS fit; asymptotically $F_{2,n-p}$ when $n>p$.

nodes.name: Elastic-net covariance statistic
nodes.statement_latex: $T_k = \bigl(\langle y, X\hat{\beta}^{\mathrm{en}}(\lambda_{k+1},\gamma)\rangle - \langle y, X_A \tilde{\beta}_A^{\mathrm{en}}(\lambda_{k+1},\gamma)\rangle\bigr)/\sigma^2$; orthogonal $X$ gives $(1+\gamma)T_k \stackrel{d}{\to} \Exp(1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Extension of the covariance statistic to the elastic net.

nodes.name: GLM/likelihood covariance statistic
nodes.statement_latex: $T_k = \bigl(\langle I_0^{-1/2} S_0, X\hat{\beta}^{\mathrm{lik}}(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle - \langle I_0^{-1/2} S_0, X_A \tilde{\beta}_A^{\mathrm{lik}}(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle\bigr)/2$ with score $S_\eta = \nabla\ell(\eta)$ and information $I_\eta = \nabla^2 \ell(\eta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Extension of $T_k$ to penalized likelihood (GLMs, Cox).

nodes.name: LARS algorithm
nodes.statement_latex: Computes the entire lasso solution path $\hat{\beta}(\lambda)$ as $\lambda$ decreases from $\infty$ to $0$, traversing the piecewise-linear knots one at a time.
nodes.statement_clean: Path algorithm tracing all lasso solutions.
output: Active sets and signs at each knot

nodes.name: Covariance test procedure
nodes.statement_latex: At each knot $\lambda_k$ along the lasso path compute $T_k$ from $X\hat{\beta}(\lambda_{k+1})$ and $X_A \tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1})$, then compare to $\Exp(1)$ for a $p$-value.
nodes.statement_clean: Sequential significance test for variables entering the lasso model.
output: Sequence of statistics $T_1, T_2, \ldots$ and $p$-values from $\Exp(1)$ (or $F_{2,n-p}$ when $\sigma^2$ is estimated)

nodes.name: Compute lasso path via LARS
nodes.statement_latex: Run the LARS algorithm on $(X,y)$ to obtain knots $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots$ together with active sets $A_k$ and signs $s_{A_k}$.

nodes.name: At each step compute $T_k$
nodes.statement_latex: For $k=1,2,\ldots$ compute $T_k = (\langle y, X\hat{\beta}(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle - \langle y, X_A \tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1})\rangle)/\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Convert to $p$-value
nodes.statement_latex: Compute $p_k = 1 - F_{\Exp(1)}(T_k) = e^{-T_k}$ (or use $F_{2,n-p}$ when $\sigma^2$ is estimated).

nodes.name: Knot form of the covariance statistic
nodes.statement_latex: If $s_A = \mathrm{sign}(\tilde{\beta}_A(\lambda_{k+1}))$ (no sign change in the reduced problem), then $T_k = C(A,s_A,j,s) \cdot \lambda_k(\lambda_k - \lambda_{k+1})/\sigma^2$, with $C(A,s_A,j,s) = \|(X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A\|_2^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under a no-sign-change condition, $T_k$ equals a product of consecutive knot values times a geometric factor.

nodes.name: Top-two spacing of $\chi_1$ order statistics
nodes.statement_latex: If $V_1 \geq V_2 \geq \cdots \geq V_p$ are the order statistics of an i.i.d. $\chi_1$ sample, then $V_1(V_1 - V_2) \stackrel{d}{\to} \Exp(1)$ as $p\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Largest $\chi_1$ order statistic times the gap to the next is asymptotically standard exponential.
assumptions: $V_1 \geq \cdots \geq V_p$ are order statistics of i.i.d. $\chi_1$ variates

nodes.name: Joint exponential limits for $\chi_1$ spacings
nodes.statement_latex: For any fixed $k\geq 1$, $(V_1(V_1-V_2),\ldots,V_k(V_k-V_{k+1})) \stackrel{d}{\to} (\Exp(1),\Exp(1/2),\ldots,\Exp(1/k))$ with independent components, where $\Exp(\alpha)$ has scale $\alpha$.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint limit of consecutive spacing statistics is independent exponentials with scales $1, 1/2, \ldots, 1/k$.
assumptions: $V_1 \geq \cdots \geq V_p$ are order statistics of i.i.d. $\chi_1$ variates

nodes.name: Dual event for argmax of $g$ (orthogonal/first step)
nodes.statement_clean: The argmax event admits a tractable dual representation involving only $g$ and $M$.
assumptions: $g, h^{(j_1,s_1)}, M$ as defined for the first step

nodes.name: Normal-tail ratio limit
nodes.statement_latex: For any $t \geq 0$, $\frac{\bar{\Phi}(u(t,m))}{\bar{\Phi}(m)} \to e^{-t}$ as $m \to \infty$, where $u(a,b) = (b + \sqrt{b^2 + 4a})/2$.
nodes.statement_clean: A ratio of standard-normal survival functions tends to the exponential tail.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition for $T_1 \to \Exp(1)$
nodes.statement_latex: If for any fixed $m_0 > 0$, $\sum_{j_1,s_1} \mathbb{P}(M(j_1,s_1) \leq m_0) \to 0$ as $p \to \infty$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_1 > t) \to e^{-t}$ for all $t \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail-control on $M$ implies the asymptotic $\Exp(1)$ distribution of $T_1$.

nodes.name: Dual event for argmax of $g$ (general step)
nodes.statement_latex: The event $\{g(j_k,s_k) > g(j,s) \text{ for all } (j,s)\neq(j_k,s_k)\}$ equals $\{g(j_k,s_k) > 0\} \cap \{g(j_k,s_k) > M^+(j_k,s_k)\} \cap \{g(j_k,s_k) < M^-(j_k,s_k)\} \cap \{0 > M^0(j_k,s_k)\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of the dual event using the triplet $(M^+, M^-, M^0)$.
assumptions: $g, M^+, M^-, M^0$ defined as in Section~4.2 with $A,s_A$ fixed
conclusions: Argmax event equals the four-fold intersection above

nodes.name: Conservative exponential limit for $\widetilde{T}_k$
nodes.statement_latex: If for any fixed $m_0$, $\sum_{j_k,s_k} \mathbb{P}(M^+(j_k,s_k) \leq m_0/\sqrt{C(j_k,s_k)}) \to 0$ as $p \to \infty$, then $\lim_{p\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(\widetilde{T}_k > t) \leq e^{-t}$ for all $t \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail control on $M^+$ gives a conservative exponential bound for the modified statistic.

nodes.name: $M^+ \leq M$ on the argmax event
nodes.statement_latex: On the event $E(j_k,s_k)$, $M^+(j_k,s_k) \leq M(j_k,s_k)$; hence under the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv2}, $\lim_{p\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(T_k > t) \leq e^{-t}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Comparison lemma transferring the bound from $\widetilde{T}_k$ to $T_k$.

nodes.name: Variance identity for $g$
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathrm{Var}(g(j,s)) = \frac{X_j^T(I-P_A)X_j \sigma^2}{[s - X_j^T(X_A^T)^+ s_A]^2} = \frac{\sigma^2}{\|(X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A\|_2^2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two equivalent formulae for the variance of $g(j,s)$ at fixed $A,s_A$.
conclusions: The variance equals both displayed expressions

nodes.name: Truncated normal-tail ratio bound
nodes.statement_latex: If $v=v(m) > m$, then $\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{\Phi(v + u(t,m) - m) - \Phi(u(t,m))}{\Phi(v) - \Phi(m)} \leq e^{-t}$ for any $t \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Truncated analogue of Lemma~\ref{lemexpratio} used in the general-step bound.

nodes.name: Recursion for $g^{(A,s_A)}$ to $g^{(A\cup\{j_k\}, s_{A\cup\{j_k\}})}$
nodes.statement_latex: $\frac{g^{(A,s_A)}(j,s) - (\Sigma_{j_k,j}/\Sigma_{j_k,j_k}) g^{(A,s_A)}(j_k,s_k)}{1 - \Sigma_{j_k,j}/\Sigma_{j_k,j_k}} = g^{(A\cup\{j_k\}, s_{A\cup\{j_k\}})}(j,s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional decorrelation identity that updates the generalized process when one variable is added.

nodes.name: Orthogonal X, general step (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement_latex: If $X^T X = I$, $y \sim N(X\beta^*, \sigma^2 I)$, $|A^*| = k_0$, and the smallest nonzero true coefficient grows faster than $\sigma\sqrt{2\log p}$, then $\mathbb{P}(B) \to 1$ and $(T_{k_0+1},\ldots,T_{k_0+d}) \stackrel{d}{\to} (\Exp(1),\Exp(1/2),\ldots,\Exp(1/d))$ as $p \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: For orthogonal $X$ with strong signals, the covariance statistic has the predicted joint exponential null distribution.

nodes.name: General X, first step (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement_latex: If $X$ has unit-norm columns in general position and there exists $\delta > 0$ and, for each $j$, a subset $S$ satisfying $1 - R_{i,S\setminus\{i\}}(R_{S\setminus\{i\},S\setminus\{i\}})^{-1} R_{S\setminus\{i\},i} \geq \delta^2$ for $i\in S$ and $|S| \geq d_p$ with $d_p/\log p \to \infty$, then under $H_0: \beta^* = 0$, $\mathbb{P}(T_1 > t) \to e^{-t}$ for all $t \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: First-step covariance statistic has an asymptotic $\Exp(1)$ null under a conditional-variance/$\log p$ condition on $X$.
assumptions: $X$ has unit-norm columns in general position

nodes.name: General X, general step (Theorem 3)
nodes.statement_latex: If $X$ has columns in general position, $\mathbb{P}(B) \to 1$ for the event $B$ in \eqref{eqgenxb}, $\|(X_{A_0})^+ X_j\|_1 \leq 1-\eta$ for $j\notin A_0$, the diagonal entries of $R_{ij}=X_i^T(I-P_{A_0})X_j$ are of comparable order, and for each $j\notin A_0$ a subset $S$ exists with $|S| \geq d_p$, $d_p/\log p \to \infty$ satisfying \eqref{eqcv2}, \eqref{eqcovvar}, \eqref{eqirrep2}, then at step $k=k_0+1$, $\lim_{p\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(T_k > t) \leq e^{-t}$ for all $t \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: General-$X$ general-step result: $T_k$ is asymptotically (conservatively) $\Exp(1)$ under irrepresentability + path-stability + conditional-variance assumptions.
conclusions: $\lim_{p\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(T_k > t) \leq e^{-t}$ for all $t \geq 0$ (also conditionally on $B$)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemcovtestknot} (knot form)
nodes.statement_latex: Use continuity of the lasso path at $\lambda_k$ to derive $(P_{A\cup\{j\}}-P_A)y = \lambda_k((X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A)$, then square and inner-product with $y$ to plug into \eqref{eqcovtestproj}.

nodes.name: Continuity identity at $\lambda_k$
nodes.statement_latex: From continuity of the lasso path: $P_A y - \lambda_k(X_A^T)^+ s_A = P_{A\cup\{j\}} y - \lambda_k(X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}}$, hence $(P_{A\cup\{j\}}-P_A)y = \lambda_k((X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A)$.

nodes.name: Square both sides
nodes.statement_latex: Using $(P_{A\cup\{j\}}-P_A)^2 = P_{A\cup\{j\}}-P_A$, obtain $y^T(P_{A\cup\{j\}}-P_A)y = \lambda_k^2 \|(X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Inner product with $y$
nodes.statement_latex: Take the inner product with $y$ and substitute the previous identity to get $y^T((X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A) = \lambda_k \|(X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T)^+ s_{A\cup\{j\}} - (X_A^T)^+ s_A\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Substitute into projection form
nodes.statement_latex: Plug the two identities into the projection form \eqref{eqcovtestproj} of $T_k$ to obtain $T_k = C(A,s_A,j,s) \lambda_k(\lambda_k - \lambda_{k+1})/\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemanytwo}
nodes.statement_latex: Apply Theorem 2.2.1 of de Haan--Ferreira (extreme value theory) to $\chi_1$ order statistics and Theorem 3 of Weissman to obtain a joint extreme-value limit; then verify $a_p/b_p \to 1$ using Mills' ratio.

nodes.name: Mills-ratio identity for $\chi_1$
nodes.statement_latex: $F(x) = (2\Phi(x)-1)\mathbf{1}\{x\geq 0\}$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty} F''(t)(1-F(t))/(F'(t))^2 = -1$ via Mills' ratio.

nodes.name: Apply EVT and Weissman
nodes.statement_latex: Theorem 2.2.1 of de Haan--Ferreira gives $b_p(V_1 - a_p) \stackrel{d}{\to} -\log E_0$; Theorem 3 of Weissman yields the joint limit $(W_0, W_1, \ldots, W_k) \stackrel{d}{\to} (-\log G_0, E_1/1, \ldots, E_k/k)$.

nodes.name: Show $a_p/b_p \to 1$
nodes.statement_latex: Using Mills' inequalities $\frac{\phi(a_p)}{a_p}\frac{1}{1+1/a_p^2} \leq 1-\Phi(a_p) \leq \frac{\phi(a_p)}{a_p}$ together with $1-\Phi(a_p) = 1/(2p)$ and $b_p = 2p\phi(a_p)$, deduce $b_p/a_p \to 1$.

nodes.name: Combine to obtain spacing limit
nodes.statement_latex: Write $V_i(V_i - V_{i+1}) = (a_p/b_p) W_i + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ and pass to the limit, yielding the joint $(\Exp(1),\Exp(1/2),\ldots,\Exp(1/k))$ distribution.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thmorthxgen}
nodes.statement_latex: First show $\mathbb{P}(B) \to 1$ using Mills-ratio bounds; then on $B$, $T_{k_0+i} = V_i(V_i-V_{i+1})$ for the $\chi_1$ order statistics of inactive coordinates, so the result follows from Lemma~\ref{lemanytwo}.

nodes.name: Choose threshold $c_p$
nodes.statement_latex: Let $\theta_p = \min_{i\in A^*} |\beta_i^*|$ and choose $c_p$ with $c_p - \sigma\sqrt{2\log p} \to \infty$ and $\theta_p - c_p \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Bound active and inactive probabilities
nodes.statement_latex: Show $\mathbb{P}(\min_{j\in A^*}|U_j| > c_p) \to 1$ and $\mathbb{P}(\max_{j\notin A^*}|U_j| \leq c_p) \to 1$, hence $\mathbb{P}(B) \to 1$.

nodes.name: Reduce $T_{k_0+i}$ to spacings on $B$
nodes.statement_latex: On $B$ (probability $\to 1$), $T_{k_0+i} = V_i(V_i - V_{i+1}) + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ for the $\chi_1$ order statistics of $|U_j|, j\notin A^*$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma~\ref{lemanytwo}
nodes.statement_latex: Conclude using the joint exponential limit for $\chi_1$ spacings.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemeventdual}
nodes.statement_latex: Show $g(j_1,s_1) > g(j,s) \Leftrightarrow g(j_1,s_1) > h^{(j_1,s_1)}(j,s)$, take intersection over $(j,s)\neq(j_1,s_1)$, and use $g(j_1,s_1)$ vs $g(j_1,-s_1)$ opposite signs together with $M(j_1,s_1) \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemexpratio}
nodes.statement_latex: By l'H\^{o}pital's rule, $\lim_{m\to\infty} \bar{\Phi}(u(t,m))/\bar{\Phi}(m) = \lim_{m\to\infty} \phi(u(t,m))/\phi(m) \cdot \partial u(t,m)/\partial m$; the first factor tends to $e^{-t}$, the second to $1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv}
nodes.statement_latex: Split the integral in \eqref{eqt1bd} at threshold $m_0$; choose $m_0$ so the integrand is $\leq \varepsilon$ on $[m_0,\infty)$; the assumption \eqref{eqmtoinf} controls the residual on $[0,m_0]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thmgenxfirst}
nodes.statement_latex: Bound $\mathbb{P}(M(j_1,s_1) \leq m_0) \leq c^{|S|}$ via an inductive argument on the joint distribution of $V_j = (U_j - R_{j,j_1}U_{j_1})/2$ for $j\in S$, using the conditional-variance bound \eqref{eqcv}; then apply Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv}.

nodes.name: Reduce $M$ to $V_j$
nodes.statement_latex: Lower-bound $M(j_1,s_1) \geq \max_{j\in S} |U_j - R_{j,j_1}U_{j_1}|/2$, so $\mathbb{P}(M(j_1,s_1)\leq m_0) \leq \mathbb{P}(|V_j| \leq m_0, j\in S)$ where $V_j = (U_j - R_{j,j_1}U_{j_1})/2$.

nodes.name: Conditional-variance bound on $V_j$
nodes.statement_latex: Use $\mathrm{Var}(U_i|U_\ell, \ell\in S\setminus\{i\}) \geq \sigma^2\delta^2$ and the law of total variance to obtain $\mathrm{Var}(V_j|U_1,\ldots,U_{j-1},U_{j_1}) \geq \sigma^2\delta^2/4$.

nodes.name: Inductive bound $\mathbb{P}(\bigcap_j\{|V_j|\leq m_0\}) \leq c^r$
nodes.statement_latex: Induct on $|S|$ with $c = \Phi(2m_0/(\sigma\delta)) - \Phi(-2m_0/(\sigma\delta)) < 1$, using independence of $V_j$ and $U_{j_1}$ at each step.

nodes.name: Sum over $j_1,s_1$ and apply Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv}
nodes.statement_latex: Conclude $\sum_{j_1,s_1} \mathbb{P}(M(j_1,s_1)\leq m_0) \leq 2p \cdot c^{d_p} \to 0$, hence by Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv}, $\mathbb{P}(T_1 > t) \to e^{-t}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemeventdual2}
nodes.statement_latex: Case-split on the sign of $1 - \Sigma_{j,j'}/\Sigma_{jj}$ (positive, negative, zero) to translate the inequalities $g(j_k,s_k) > g(j,s)$ into the four inequalities involving $M^+, M^-, M^0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv2}
nodes.statement_latex: Use the dual representation, the identity $\sigma_k^2 = \Var(g(j_k,s_k))$ from Lemma~\ref{lemg2cov2}, and Lemma~\ref{lemexpratio2} to bound $\mathbb{P}(\widetilde{T}_k > t) - e^{-t}$ uniformly via $\varepsilon$-arguments.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv3}
nodes.statement_latex: Use the recursion of Lemma~\ref{lemg3} to identify $M^+(j_k,s_k) = \max_{(j,s)\in S^+} g^{(A\cup\{j_k\}, s_{A\cup\{j_k\}})}(j,s)$, then on $E(j_k,s_k)$ bound this by $M(j_k,s_k)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thmgenxgen}
nodes.statement_latex: Mirror the proof of Theorem~\ref{thmgenxfirst}: show $S^+(j_k,s_k) \supseteq S \times \{-1,1\}^{|S|}$ via \eqref{eqcovvar}, lower-bound $M^+$ by $V_j = (U_j - \theta_{j_k,j} U_{j_k})/2$, induct using \eqref{eqcv2} to get $\mathbb{P}(M^+(j_k,s_k) \leq m_0\sigma_k) \leq c^{|S|}$, and apply Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv3}.

nodes.name: Show $S^+(j_k,s_k)$ contains $S\times\{-1,1\}$
nodes.statement_latex: From $|R_{j,j_k}|/R_{j_k,j_k} < \eta/(2-\eta)$ and $\|(X_{A_0})^+ X_{j_k}\|_1 \leq 1-\eta$, deduce $\Sigma_{j_k,j}/\Sigma_{j_k,j_k} < 1$ for all $j\in S, s\in\{-1,1\}$.

nodes.name: Lower-bound $M^+$
nodes.statement_latex: Use $\|(X_{A_0\cup\{j_k\}})^+ X_j\|_1 < 1$ to obtain $M^+(j_k,s_k) \geq \max_{j\in S} |U_j - \theta_{j_k,j} U_{j_k}|/2 = \max_{j\in S} |V_j|$.

nodes.name: Inductive bound on joint $\{|V_j|\leq m_0\sigma_k\}$
nodes.statement_latex: Induct using $\sigma_k^2/(\sigma^2 R_{ii}) \leq C/\eta^2$ and the conditional-variance lower bound \eqref{eqcv2}, with constant $c = \Phi(2m_0\sqrt{C}/(\delta\eta)) - \Phi(-2m_0\sqrt{C}/(\delta\eta)) < 1$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv3}
nodes.statement_latex: Sum yields $\sum \mathbb{P}(M^+(j_k,s_k)\leq m_0\sigma_k) \leq 2p\cdot c^{d_p} \to 0$; conclude via Lemma~\ref{lemexpconv3}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemg2cov2}
nodes.statement_latex: Compute $z = (X_{A\cup\{j\}}^T X_{A\cup\{j\}})^{-1} s_{A\cup\{j\}}$ in block form, solve the linear system, and identify the resulting expression with $[s - X_j^T(X_A^T)^+ s_A]^2 / (X_j^T(I-P_A)X_j)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemexpratio2}
nodes.statement_latex: Use the Taylor bound $u(t,m) \geq m + t/m - t^2/m^3$, the monotonicity $u(t,w) - w \leq u(t,m) - m$ for $w\geq m$, and a change-of-variable that produces $e^{-t}$ times an integrand $\to 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemg3}
nodes.statement_latex: Match the numerators and denominators in the LHS expression to those of $g^{(A\cup\{j_k\}, s_{A\cup\{j_k\}})}(j,s)$ using the partial-regression identity $\theta_{j_k,j} = [(X_{A\cup\{j_k\}})^+ X_j]_{j_k}$.

nodes.name: Prostate cancer data
nodes.statement_latex: $n=67$ observations, $p=8$ predictors. Both forward stepwise and the lasso enter the same predictors in the same order; lasso $p$-values from the covariance test (with $\hat{\sigma}^2$) are much larger than forward-stepwise $p$-values, entering only one or two predictors at level $0.05$ (vs. four).
nodes.statement_clean: Real-data illustration on the prostate cancer dataset showing the covariance test is more conservative than the forward-stepwise chi-squared test.

nodes.name: Forward-stepwise null QQ plot (Figure 1)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=10$ orthogonal predictors, $\beta^* = 0$. The drop-in-RSS statistic $R_1$ at the first forward-stepwise step has type-I error $\approx 39\%$ at the nominal $5\%$ $\chi_1^2$ cutoff $3.84$, while $T_1$ for the lasso matches $\Exp(1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Synthetic example demonstrating that the chi-squared test is invalid for adaptive selection while the covariance test is well-calibrated.

nodes.name: Orthogonal-X simulation (Figures 2, 3)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=10$ orthogonal predictors with three nonzero coefficients equal to $6$ and $\sigma^2=1$. The covariance statistic at the 4th step is well-approximated by $\Exp(1)$, while at the 5th, 6th, 7th steps it follows $\Exp(1/2), \Exp(1/3), \Exp(1/4)$ in line with Theorem~\ref{thmorthxgen}.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulation confirming the joint exponential limits at successive lasso steps in the orthogonal case.

nodes.name: General-X null simulation (Tables 2-3)
nodes.statement_latex: Equal-data, equal-population, $\AR(1)$, and block-diagonal correlation structures with $\rho \in [0,0.8]$ and various $(n,p)$. Mean and tail probabilities of $T_1$ (and $T_{k+1}$ after $k$ true variables enter) match the $\Exp(1)$ approximation.
nodes.statement_clean: Multi-design simulation showing the $\Exp(1)$ approximation is reasonable across correlation structures.

nodes.name: Power comparison (Figure 4)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=10$ i.i.d. $N(0,1)$ predictors, $\sigma^2=1$. Power curves for the covariance test (lasso) and drop-in-RSS test (forward stepwise) using simulation- and $\Exp(1)$-based cutpoints are similar, though forward-stepwise cutpoints are not typically available in practice.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulated power study comparing the lasso covariance test to forward stepwise.

nodes.name: Unknown $\sigma^2$ simulation (Table 4)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=80$ with $\AR(1)$ predictor correlation $\rho^{|j-j'|}$ for $\rho\in\{0,0.8\}$, true model null. The $F_{2,n-p}$ approximation for $F_1$ outperforms $\Exp(1)$ when $\sigma^2$ is estimated by the full-model MSE.
nodes.statement_clean: Validates the $F_{2,n-p}$ null distribution when $\sigma^2$ is plugged in.

nodes.name: Wine data (UCI)
nodes.statement_latex: $n = 1599$, $p=11$ predictors, randomly split 500 times into training/test. Forward stepwise enters 6 predictors at the $0.05$ level whereas the covariance test enters only 3, in agreement with the elbow in test-set prediction error.
nodes.statement_clean: Real-data application to wine quality showing the more parsimonious model selected by the covariance test agrees with prediction-error elbow.

nodes.name: HIV NRTI data (Rhee et al. 2003)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=1057$ samples, $p=217$ mutation sites for the NRTI drug 3TC; 50 random splits into training/test of size 150 and 907. With $\hat{\sigma}^2$ estimated via cross-validation, the covariance test indicates only one or two important predictors, confirmed by test-set error.
nodes.statement_clean: High-dimensional ($p > n$) real-data application validating parsimony of the covariance test.

nodes.name: Logistic-regression covariance test (Figure 8)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=10$ predictors i.i.d. $N(0,1)$. QQ plots of $T_k$ at first/second steps versus $\Exp(1)$ for binary logistic regression show good agreement.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical evidence that the covariance test extends to penalized logistic regression.

nodes.name: Cox-model covariance test (Figure 9)
nodes.statement_latex: Same setup as Figure 8 but for $\ell_1$-penalized Cox proportional hazards. QQ plots vs $\Exp(1)$ are reasonably accurate.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical evidence that the covariance test extends to the Cox model.

nodes.name: Elastic-net covariance test (Figure 7)
nodes.statement_latex: $n=100$, $p=10$, orthogonal and correlated predictors (population correlation 0.5), $\gamma\in\{$small, medium, large$\}$. The distribution of $(1+\gamma)T_1$ under $\beta^*=0$ is close to $\Exp(1)$ across cases.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical evidence that the rescaled statistic for the elastic net has approximately $\Exp(1)$ null distribution.

nodes.name: Multiple testing / FDR control (Remark 1)
nodes.statement_latex: The covariance test could form the basis for multiple-testing and false-discovery-rate control procedures along the lasso path; left for future work.

nodes.name: Re-entry of variables (Remark 2)
nodes.statement_latex: For general $X$, a predictor may enter the active set more than once along the lasso path; each entry is treated as a separate test.

nodes.name: Centering for an intercept (Remark 3)
nodes.statement_latex: Centering $y$ and the columns of $X$ accommodates an intercept; centering induces correlations between residuals but $\mathrm{Cov}(X_i^T \tilde{\varepsilon}, X_j^T \tilde{\varepsilon}) = \sigma^2 X_i^T X_j$ is unchanged, so the asymptotic theory still applies.

nodes.name: Sequential nature of the test (Remark 4)
nodes.statement_latex: The covariance test is sequential along the path; testing the significance of any active predictor at a fixed $\lambda$ is harder and discussed in Section~\ref{secdiscussion}.

nodes.name: Recovering Theorem 2 from Theorem 3 (Remark 11)
nodes.statement_latex: Setting $k_0=0$, $A_0=\varnothing$ in Theorem~\ref{thmgenxgen} reduces conditions \eqref{eqirrep},\eqref{eqcv2}--\eqref{eqirrep2} to those of Theorem~\ref{thmgenxfirst} and recovers (a conservative version of) the same exponential limit.

nodes.name: Orthogonal X as special case (Remark 12)
nodes.statement_latex: For orthogonal $X$, the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thmgenxgen} are trivially satisfied (e.g., taking $S = \{1,\ldots,p\}\setminus(A_0\cup\{j\})$), and Theorem~\ref{thmorthxgen} provides the exact (non-conservative) exponential limit.

nodes.name: Conditional-variance interpretation (Remark 13)
nodes.statement_latex: Conditions \eqref{eqcv2}-\eqref{eqsgrow2} require, for each $j\notin A_0$, a subset $S$ of weakly correlated $U_i = X_i^T(I-P_{A_0})y$ of size $\gg \log p$, implying $n/\log p \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Connection to irrepresentability (Remark 14)
nodes.statement_latex: Condition \eqref{eqirrep} is the strong irrepresentability / mutual incoherence condition used in lasso support-recovery theory; here we do not require lower bounds on the magnitudes of true coefficients but assume directly that the lasso converges to a fixed $A_0, s_{A_0}$.

nodes.name: Allowing $A_0$ to contain only strong coefficients (Remark 15)
nodes.statement_latex: The arguments can be modified to allow $A_0$ to be the set of large (rather than all) nonzero coefficients of $\beta^*$, with the small ones small enough that the mean of $g$ dominates $M^+$; the details are deferred to future work.

nodes.name: Significance testing at fixed $\lambda$
nodes.statement_latex: Given a lasso fit at a fixed $\lambda$, design a significance test for each predictor in the active set (not just the one entering at a knot).
nodes.statement_clean: Open: a generic-lasso significance test for an arbitrary $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Estimation of $\sigma^2$ when $p \geq n$
nodes.statement_latex: Develop principled estimators of $\sigma^2$ in the high-dimensional setting $p \geq n$ that yield valid covariance-test $p$-values.

nodes.name: Asymptotic $\Exp(1)$ null for GLM/Cox covariance statistic
nodes.statement_latex: For penalized generalized linear models and the $\ell_1$-penalized Cox model, the covariance statistic $T_k$ in \eqref{eqcovtestglm}/\eqref{eqcovtestlik} satisfies $T_k \stackrel{d}{\to} \Exp(1)$ under $H_0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conjectured asymptotic $\Exp(1)$ null distribution for the GLM/Cox extension; supported by simulations but not proven.
